keys.label: Five keys

items.h: Jadan Baugh has to be Superman
items.p: Eddie Gilley’s first key: the back hailed as the best in the country and a Heisman contender has to charge the hole instead of dancing, if Florida is going to win in the Bluegrass state.

items.h: The offensive line has to move the Wildcats
items.p: Gilley wants better than the last two weeks: movement in the run game, no defensive linemen living in the backfield, and a center and quarterback on the same page on protections.

items.h: Eric Singleton has to be the playmaker
items.p: Injuries have slowed the receiver promised as the dynamic playmaker. Gilley says offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner has to find ways to get him the ball in space.

items.h: Aaron Philo has to be boring
items.p: Philo takes back the starting job. Gilley’s ask: the solid decision maker he was early in the season, a game manager who cannot give the game away.

items.h: The defense needs a takeaway or two
items.p: Stingy in the second half of the last two games, Gilley says, but Kentucky does not give it up often. One or two takeaways and a short field could send the Gators home with a win.

keys.source: Eddie Gilley, Keys To The Game (GatorBait Media, Nov. 13).

lead.label: The Soothsayer
lead.title: Kentucky no longer fears the Gators
lead.html:
There was a time and not all that long ago when Florida football fans measured the Kentucky game by “how much.” Never was it “will we beat Kentucky” because they were the “Mildcats” and an automatic cure for whatever ailed the Gators. A win was assured so the only question was by how much.

From 1986 until a fateful night in The Swamp in 2018, Kentucky was a mortal lock to lose to the Florida Gators. Thirty-one straight years the Gators inflicted pain on UK. Yes, there were some close calls but they were like teasers. There was the “Doering’s got a touchdown! Doering’s got a touchdown!” game that immortalized Mick Huber in the minds and hearts of Gator fans everywhere. That night in 1993 was the night the legend of Danny Wuerffel was born, but it was also the coming out party for former walk-on wide receiver Chris Doering, who would go on to set an SEC record for career touchdown receptions that stood for nearly 30 years.

We call that game a teaser because the next year, almost as if he felt the need to atone for a close call win over UK in Lexington, Steve Spurrier and the Gators wore out the Wildcats to the tune of 73-7. For years, it seemed that every time Kentucky made Florida hearts skip a beat, the Wildcats were in for a severe beating the next year.

Then came the night that will live forever in infamy. The Swamp, September 8, 2018, Dan Mullen’s second game as Florida’s head coach. The unthinkable happened. Kentucky ran for 303 yards. On the last play of the game came the ultimate insult. Feleipe Franks fumbled and Kentucky’s Davonte Robinson scooped up the loose ball, ran it in 30 yards for a TD. Kentucky 27, Florida 16.

The fear factor went poof in the humid Florida night and it has never returned. Kentucky no longer fears the Florida Gators. The Wildcats have won five of the last eight meetings with the Gators. Jon Sumrall was the defensive coordinator when Kentucky beat the Gators 20-13 in Lexington in 2021. Brad White was the defensive coordinator at UK when the Wildcats scored wins in 2022, 2023 and last year when Kentucky picked off DJ Lagway three times en route to a 38-7 humiliation of the Gators in Lexington.

Sumrall is Florida’s head coach now and White is his defensive coordinator. Tonight (6:15 p.m., ESPN) they find out if you can indeed go home again. Kentucky (7-2, 5-2 SEC) is ranked 13th nationally and very much in contention for a berth in the College Football Playoff. If the Wildcats win out in their last three games they are almost assured of the playoff. Who would have ever thought Kentucky would make the playoff much less do it before the Florida Gators?

But it could happen unless the Gators pull one out of the wazzoo. To do it they’ll be without Vernell Brown III for a sixth straight game and with Aaron Philo returning as the starting QB after Tramell Jones Jr.’s bad day at the office last week against Oklahoma.

Kentucky is a 3.5-point favorite. It seems like it should be a wider spread considering the way UK has played all year and the way the Gators have cratered since September. For Kentucky this isn’t the Super Bowl but it’s close because winning is one step closer to college football’s promised land. For Florida, a win could reverse the trend of four losses in five games and would assure the Gators of bowl eligibility.

High stakes drama in Lexington in which the team that commits the fewest turnovers is likely to pull out a win.

The Sayer Says Sooth!: The SEC Soothsayer knows all too well what a win would mean for Sumrall and White, not to mention the shot of feel good the Gators need so desperately. He is also keenly aware that Kentucky fans are ready to say screw the SEC and it’s big fines, it’s time to storm the field if the Wildcats are ahead when the clock flatlines at zero. Thirty-two years of Florida fear factor are relics of a past that Sumrall wants to resurrect. If you gamble, bet the ranch that Sumrall will restore Florida’s dignity, just not this night. The Soothsayer thinks it’s a chest clutcher Kentucky win. It’s still hard to fathom.
